payload.probes:
Seven assumptions probed against the real services (run-bfd564ff9add). All PASS, and one design figure is refined by measurement.

A1 - the brief can be made unreadable at rest. PROBE: AES-256-GCM encrypt, then search the ciphertext for a unique marker planted in the plaintext. RESULT: absent. PASS - R5's mechanism works.

A2 - the store still accepts writes. PROBE: authenticated PUT to the §18 namespace with expiration_ttl. RESULT: HTTP 200. PASS - the token recorded in July is still valid, and R7's bounded expiry is accepted by the API.

A3 - EVENTUAL CONSISTENCY, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. PROBE: poll the serve URL from the moment of the PUT until it answers 200. RESULT: 1067 ms. PASS, and it REFINES the design document: §18 records ~60s to edge, which set the expectation that notifying immediately was dangerous. The hazard is real but the window is about a second here, so read-after-write stays required (R6) while the retry budget can be small. Recording the measurement rather than the folklore.

A4 - the page RENDERS rather than downloads. PROBE: read the content-type off the serve response. RESULT: text/html; charset=utf-8. PASS - this is the exact property the design says anonymous paste hosts fail, and it is why this host was chosen.

A5 - the host holds ciphertext. PROBE: fetch the stored object and search for the plaintext marker. RESULT: absent. PASS - R5 verified from the outside, not merely intended.

A6 - the card can carry the ladder's shape. PROBE: publish a three-action card - two http answers plus one view link - to a THROWAWAY topic, so the owner's phone was not disturbed. RESULT: HTTP 200 with all three actions accepted, shapes http/http/view. PASS - R3's budget and R1's absolute URLs are both satisfiable, and this is the exact structure v1 uses.

A7 - a gate can look like a gate. PROBE: check that title, priority 4 and the bangbang tag survive the round trip. RESULT: all three intact. PASS - R2 is achievable.

RAID UPDATE: R3 (eventual consistency) is downgraded from a risk to a measured, bounded behaviour - read-after-write stays, the retry window shrinks. R5 (the host going away) is unchanged but now has a live datum: the account, worker, namespace and token all still function four days after they were set up. Nothing here touches R1's corrected confidentiality claim, which is about the relay rather than the host. NOT PROBED, and it cannot be: how the card and the page actually render on the phone, and whether the tap fires - that is D1, and it is the owner's release-gate bless.
